evals.name: happy-path-sync
evals.prompt: Can you run the upstream sync and see if anything new came in? If there's a PR, tell me what's in it and whether it's ready to merge.
evals.expected_output: Triggers the Upstream Sync workflow, watches it to completion, checks for an auto-opened PR, reports PR number/URL/diff-stat if one exists, or 'no new upstream' if not. Correctly uses `--repo zjean/server` flag, does NOT push to upstream-main directly, does NOT target Sync-in/server for the PR.

evals.name: conflict-resolution
evals.prompt: The upstream-sync workflow just opened PR #99 on zjean/server and it's CONFLICTING. Get it merged.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that upstream-main is workflow-writable only, closes PR #99 with a superseded comment, branches off main, merges origin/upstream-main into it with --no-ff, resolves conflicts (correctly prefers upstream for overlapping i18n keys, preserves our custom keys), runs builds to verify, pushes the new branch, opens a replacement PR targeting zjean/server with merge-commit strategy noted in the body.

evals.name: investigate-custom-ui-impact
evals.prompt: An upstream sync just merged into main. It touched some backend/src/applications/files/ code. Do we need to update anything in our custom v2/v3 UI, and if so what exactly?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the upstream commits via `git log origin/main..origin/upstream-main` or equivalent, diffs each interesting commit, classifies changes as wire-contract / internal-refactor / behaviour-change, greps custom-v2/ and shared classic services for callers, produces a scannable report with concrete before/after patches where wire contracts changed, and a 'No impact' section or explicit recommendations. Does NOT silently apply edits — the investigation is the deliverable.
